newsitem.title: USA: Bloomberg says it won't buy Dow Jones unit.
newsitem.headline: Bloomberg says it won't buy Dow Jones unit.

text.p: Bloomberg LP founder Michael Bloomberg says his financial news and information company is not interested in buying the Dow Jones Markets (formerly Telerate) division of its rival, Dow Jones & Co.
"We are builders, not buyers," Bloomberg told the PBS news magazine program, TechnoPolitics, in an interview to be aired this weekend.

"When you buy something, you inheret their problems as well as their strengths," Bloomberg said. "Inheriting 2,000-odd people that work for that part of the company -- that would change our culture. Remember, they (Dow Jones Markets) have a culture that doesn't really work. That's why it's for sale."
Bloomberg has been rumored as a potential buyer for Dow Jones Markets, which provides electronic information and competes with services provided by both Bloomberg and Reuters Holdings Plc.

The unit's operating income tumbled 83.8 percent in the first quarter to $7.5 million. Dow Jones said earlier this year it would invest up to $650 million to revitalize the unit. The company's shareholders have said they want the company to sell the unit rather than spend the money.
